purpose: Determine whether final visual.proj adds task dependence to the previously fixed local block support before designing a joint defense. Necessary-condition diagnostic on unprotected experts, not a new protection or successful recovery attack on a new release.
access: Only target expert and public pretrained weights define each erasure. Reuse historical target-label-selected regions, unchanged and without partners. No calibration images, teacher queries, fitting, gradients, rank or amplitude search. The other seven experts enter only the fixed evaluator.
protocol: Reset visual.proj alone, three entire residual blocks (Attention including Q/K, MLP and LayerNorm) alone, or their union to the public anchor. Keep all other target parameters unchanged. Measure native target and MNIST/SVHN/Cars/DTD of author eight-expert Task Arithmetic at0.2. Reuse audited original fusion arrays, measure each native baseline. Previously inspected tests are diagnostic; no fresh held-out defense claim.
interpretation: For a release changing only a supportS, public erasure yields the same erased state as the original iff all changed coordinates are erased. Each measured fusion score is then a conditional feasible recovery floor on this fixed pool. A lower floor is necessary for that support to be useful, not evidence of an effective defense or hard recovery. It does not cover changes outside the support, altered architectures, or arbitrary partners.
reporting: 48 complete evaluations and12 reused baseline rows. Nine independent coordinate-mask checks plus all60 prediction count/pair and128-image-prefix replays. Raw arrays stay on server; only config, source, hashes and summaries local/GitHub. Four evaluated tasks, no EuroSAT test or eight-task average. No protection construction follows automatically.
